  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.65»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.65

by J. G. Thompson

Conjecture: $\frac{p^q-1}{p-1}$ never divides $\frac{q^p-1}{q-1}$ if $p$, $q$ are
distinct primes.

The notebook remarks that the validity of this conjecture would simplify the proof of
solvability of groups of odd order (W. Feit, J. G. Thompson, *Pacific J. Math.* **13**,
no. 3 (1963), 775–1029), rendering unnecessary the detailed use of generators and
relations. This is the Feit–Thompson conjecture on primes; see also
`FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture.lean`.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 4.65
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feit%E2%80%93Thompson_conjecture)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.65»

/--
Conjecture: $\frac{p^q-1}{p-1}$ never divides $\frac{q^p-1}{q-1}$ if $p$, $q$ are
distinct primes.

Both quotients are natural numbers, since $p - 1$ divides $p^q - 1$ and $q - 1$ divides
$q^p - 1$; hence the natural-number division here is exact.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.65» (p q : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    ¬ (p ^ q - 1) / (p - 1) ∣ (q ^ p - 1) / (q - 1) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.65»

modeling_decisions: Used ℕ truncated subtraction and floor division `(p ^ q - 1) / (p - 1)` verbatim from the source (matching FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/FeitThompsonPrimeConjecture.lean) rather than the geometric sum `∑ i ∈ range q, p ^ i`; the two agree because p - 1 ∣ p ^ q - 1 and p ≥ 2 for prime p, so no default-value artifact arises.
Distinctness stated as `p ≠ q` (both orderings), not `p < q`; this is the literal reading of the notebook and is equivalent to the p < q form by relabeling.
AMS tags 11 20: number theory for the statement itself, group theory for the notebook's stated motivation (Feit–Thompson odd-order theorem). A reviewer may prefer AMS 11 alone.
The sentence about simplifying the Feit–Thompson proof is treated as motivation and recorded only in the docstrings, not formalized.

Natural-number division is exact since p - 1 ∣ p^q - 1 for prime p (p ≥ 2, so truncated subtraction is also harmless). Quantifies over both orderings of distinct primes, as the decomposition table requires; the source is a conjecture rather than a yes/no question, so the plain Prop form is used (no answer(sorry)).
